subject: Deterministic tail-latency addendum request — Dedicated pool (Aurora Edge)
content:
From: Alex R. <alex.r@aurora-edge.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwoodai.com
Cc: procurement@aurora-edge.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: deterministic tail-latency addendum for dedicated pool

Kimberly —

Thanks for the rapid onboarding last month. We're close to go-live but our SREs are pushing for stronger guarantees around tail latency (95th/99th) during sustained adversarial bursts. Our procurement team asked me to open an addendum request to the Dedicated Capacity contract that specifies:

- A deterministic 95th percentile token latency target for requests up to 2k tokens
- A 99th percentile target with a defined mitigation plan if breached
- Clear queueing behavior during temporary oversubscription (how requests are prioritized, preemption rules, and a bounded retry/backoff policy)

I've attached our SLO matrix and a first-pass redline of language we think will be acceptable. Can you confirm operational feasibility and whether Redwood can commit to deterministic tail bounds for our reserved GPU pool? If not, what mitigations (burst credits, warm standby, prioritized KV cache) can you provide?

Attachments: [Attachment: aurora_slo_matrix.xlsx (XLSX)]

Thanks,
Alex R.
Head of Platform
Aurora Edge

-----------------------------------------

From: kimberly_park@redwoodai.com
To: Alex R. <alex.r@aurora-edge.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodai.com, marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:05:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: deterministic tail-latency addendum for dedicated pool

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask and the SLO matrix. Short answer: we don't offer absolute determinism for 99th percentile in the general sense (due to hardware and multi-tenant transient factors), but for a reserved pool we can provide a contract addendum that: 

1) Guarantees 95th percentile token latency targets for the specified workload envelope (2k tokens, baseline concurrency) when reservation and warm-standby sizing is agreed.
2) Defines a 99th percentile objective with an operational remediation ladder (automatic burst-capacity activation, priority queueing, and per-incident crediting) rather than an unconditional hard SLA.
3) Specifies queueing semantics under oversubscription: a) reserved capacity requests are isolated to the Dedicated pool, b) requests above the customer's committed concurrency are throttled with exponential backoff and transparent retry headers, c) preemption is applied to lower-tier burst traffic first.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben, can you confirm pricing/credits behavior for the burst and warm-standby plan?
- Marissa, ops: can you validate the 95th-latency numbers from our staging runs and draft the mitigation playbook language that maps to the 99th remediation ladder?

If you're open, I'll draft an addendum (legal-ready) that captures the guaranteed 95th bound plus a 99th remediation ladder and run it by our contracts team.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: draft-addendum-v2.docx referenced]

-----------------------------------------

On Mon, May 10, 2027 at 12:32 PM -0700, ben_carter@redwoodai.com wrote:
From: ben_carter@redwoodai.com
To: kimberly_park@redwoodai.com, Alex R. <alex.r@aurora-edge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 12:32:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: deterministic tail-latency addendum for dedicated pool

Alex / Kim —

Quick technical addendum from infra/sales side: we ran a 72-hr soak with Aurora-like traffic patterns in our east region on a dedicated 8-GPU pool with warm-standby (1.2x capacity) and saw:

- 95th token latency: 42–55 ms (2k token prompts) under baseline concurrency (up to 320 concurrent requests)
- 99th token latency: 210–380 ms during adversarial bursts (sustained >1.5x concurrent load for >3m); these spikes correlated with KV cache priming and cross-GPU synchronization during large context windows

Operational mitigations we can commit in the addendum:
- Auto-burst activation: 10-minute cold-start window for additional nodes to spin up with a documented runbook
- Priority queueing: guaranteed faster path for pinned tenant tokens (reservation-based) and documented shunting of non-critical requests
- KV cache warmpreload: option to pre-warm top-XX prefixes before expected launches (requires data pre-provisioning)

I suggest the addendum commit to the observed 95th number range as a contractual target and include the 99th remediation ladder we discussed (activation, credits, root-cause postmortem). For strict procurement language, we can include an objective/measurement appendix that references our tracing IDs and the measurement window.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

-----------------------------------------

On Wed, May 12, 2027 at 16:02:00 -0700, kimberly_park@redwoodai.com wrote:
From: kimberly_park@redwoodai.com
To: Alex R. <alex.r@aurora-edge.com>, ben_carter@redwoodai.com, marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: deterministic tail-latency addendum for dedicated pool

Alex —

Thanks for the patience. We've prepared a draft addendum that: 

- Guarantees a 95th percentile token latency target of <= 60 ms for requests up to 2k tokens under agreed reservation and warm-standby configuration (definition and measurement methodology included).
- Establishes a 99th percentile objective (<= 400 ms) and an explicit remediation ladder: Tier 1 auto-burst (minutes), Tier 2 manual capacity re-allocation (hours), Tier 3 credits/financial remediation if systemic after RCA.
- Specifies queueing semantics: reserved pool isolation, preemption order, explicit retry headers (x-redwood-retry-after), and a bounded client backoff guideline.

I've attached the legal-ready draft (v2) and a measurement appendix. If this aligns, I'll route to Legal and send you a DocuSign link for signature. If you want harder 99th guarantees, we can discuss a higher committed capacity or extended warm-standby (pricing impact).

Next milestones:
- Aurora: review draft addendum and SLO appendix (please flag redlines) — target response by Fri 05/14
- Redwood (Ben/Marissa): finalize pricing language for warm-standby and burst credits by EOD 05/13
- Legal: we will prep the DocuSign envelope once Aurora confirms

DocuSign preview: https://docusign.com/embedded?envelopeId=0A12B3C4D5
HubSpot record: https://hubspot.com/contacts/AE-2027-07-DED-21

Best,
Kimberly
